title: UN Scientists: AI Is Threatening Natural Resources for Billions
excerpt: Artificial Intelligence's environmental footprint is expanding at a pace that could strain the planet’s natural resources.
content_html:
By 2030, AI’s water use will match the needs of 1.3 billion people while its power use triples that of 650 million, UN University investigation warns

Richmond Hill, Ontario, Canada (3 June 2026) – By 2030, the global data centres powering artificial intelligence are projected to consume 945 terawatt-hours of electricity. This is nearly triple the combined annual electricity use of Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Nigeria—countries collectively home to more than 650 million people. Their associated water footprint will equal the basic annual domestic water needs of all 1.3 billion people in Sub-Saharan Africa, and their land footprint will exceed 14,500 square kilometers, roughly twice the Jakarta metropolitan area, home to more than 32 million people.

These stark findings are detailed in the new report, Environmental Cost of AI’s Energy Use: Carbon, Water and Land Footprints, by the United Nations University Institute for Water, Environment and Health (UNU-INWEH). Researchers have previously warned about the greenhouse gas emissions of data centers before. But the UN scientists now argue that the environmental costs of AI and data centers cannot be understood through carbon emissions alone. In their report, they quantify the carbon, water and land footprints of AI’s electricity use across the globe and highlight the big differences between these footprints in the world’s 20 largest data center hubs.

“This report is not a case against artificial intelligence, a technological transformation that is improving the lives of billions of people around the world,” said Professor Kaveh Madani, Director of UNU-INWEH who led the investigation team. “It is a call for using it responsibly and addressing its unintended impacts proactively to make it sustainable and equitable. We have a narrow window to ensure that the backbone of the technological revolution of our era develops within planetary limits, and that the communities who provide the critical minerals for advancing AI and the ones that host its infrastructure and e-waste are also among those who benefit from it.” 

A footprint that is being mismeasured

The report finds that AI’s environmental cost is being systematically mismeasured. Most existing assessments focus on the carbon emissions associated with training large models. Yet every kilowatt-hour of electricity used to train or run an AI system also carries a water footprint, from cooling and power generation, and a land footprint, from energy infrastructure and supply chains. These three footprints do not move in the same direction. Switching from coal to bioenergy, for example, can on average cut the carbon footprint of electricity by 70 per cent, while increasing its water footprint more than thirty-fold and its land footprint a hundred-fold. The report concludes that “low-carbon” is not automatically “low-water” or “low-land” and warns that evaluating AI sustainability through a single metric can hide trade-offs and shift environmental burdens onto regions already facing water or land stress.

The numbers compound rapidly at the infrastructure level. Global data centres consumed an estimated 448 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2025. If treated as a nation, they would have been the world’s 11th largest electricity consumer, behind France and ahead of Saudi Arabia.

“What surprised us most is how often the choices that look greenest from a carbon perspective end up worse for water or for land,” said Dr. Miriam Aczel, UNU-INWEH Researcher and the lead author of the report. “If we keep judging AI sustainability by carbon alone, we might think that renewables make AI infrastructure clean but that is solving one problem while creating other problems, often in places that didn’t ask for it.”

Inference, efficiency, and the rebound effect

Public discussion has largely focused on the energy required to train massive models. Training GPT-3 was estimated to require 1.3 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of electricity, while estimates suggest GPT-4 consumed between 50 and 70 GWh. However, the report reveals this framing is outdated. Once a model is deployed, inference—the continuous running of models to answer everyday user prompts—becomes the dominant cost, accounting for 80 to 90 per cent of total AI energy use. ChatGPT alone is estimated to process around 2.5 billion prompts per day, translating to roughly 383 GWh of electricity per year for a single product. Offsetting associated carbon emissions would require 2.6 million tree seedlings grown for 10 years, enough trees to cover a land area the size of Manhattan. The water footprint is equivalent to the minimum annual domestic water needs of roughly 500,000 people in Sub-Saharan Africa, and the land footprint is equal to over 800 football fields.

Video generation as an emerging environmental crisis

Per-query energy varies by orders of magnitude depending on the task. A typical conversational chat query is around 200 times more energy-intensive than basic text classification. Generating a single AI image can require around 1,450 times that baseline. A single short AI-generated video can consume as much electricity as 200,000 spam classifications. Model choice, prompt length, output format and resolution all materially shape the footprint. Yet most of these decisions are taken invisibly, by product defaults the user never sees.

The report invokes the rebound effect (the Jevons Paradox), warning that as models become more efficient, they become cheaper and are used more frequently. Without explicit limits on tokens, resolution, or default output length, improvements at the per-query level are easily wiped out by sheer volume growth.

“A lot of people think that the environmental footprint of AI reduces, as technology improves and processes become more efficient. But that is only a partial picture of the overall problem,” said Professor Madani, a co-author of the report who was recently named the 2026 Stockholm Water Prize Laureate. “More efficient and affordable AI and energy mean more consumption of AI, making the overall footprint far bigger than what we save through efficiency gains.”

Local costs, distant benefits

The benefits and burdens of the massive global expansion of AI are highly unequal. Several site-level cases in the report show how globally distributed AI services create intense local pressures. In Ireland, data centres accounted for 21% of total metered electricity in 2023, exceeding all urban households. The national grid operator has paused new approvals around Dublin until 2028, making Ireland a concrete, documented example of what happens when AI infrastructure growth outpaces energy planning — and a preview of what other countries are heading toward.

In Querétaro, Mexico, expanding compute infrastructure is drawing on water supplies amid prolonged droughts. In Uruguay, plans for a water-intensive data centre coincided with a 2023 drought that depleted Montevideo’s freshwater reserves, making tap water unsafe to drink.

Furthermore, AI infrastructure could generate up to 2.5 million tonnes of electronic waste each year by 2030, much of it processed in low-income economies with limited safeguards, while critical minerals are extracted in jurisdictions with weak environmental oversight.

“If you map where data centres are getting built against where water stress is worst, you tend to see the same regions in some instances,” said Dr. Mir Matin, Manager of UNU-INWEH’s Geospatial, Climate and Infrastructure Analytics Programme and a co-author of the report. “And the communities living near these sites are not necessarily the ones using the AI being run there. That asymmetry is the issue. Without fixing it, we’ll just be repeating older patterns, where some places carry the costs and other places capture the benefits.”

The digital divide: AI computing is 90% concentrated in two countries

While the AI infrastructure comes with environmental costs, they also have major economic, security and sovereignty advantages that encourage the wealthier countries to build more data centers. Only 32 countries in the world host AI-specialised data centres, and 90% of that capacity is concentrated in 2 countries, while more than 150 countries currently have little or no access to sovereign AI compute. The report frames this not just as an economic divide but as an environmental justice issue: excluded countries bear critical minerals extraction and e-waste burdens while the strategic benefits flow elsewhere.

“The global system building artificial intelligence must also govern it sustainably and fairly,” said Professor Tshilidzi Marwala, Rector of the United Nations University and Under-Secretary-General of the United Nations. “The concentrated development of AI infrastructure in the privileged areas of the world is creating a large digital divide that poses profound challenges in the equitable development of AI. AI can certainly advance prosperity and human well-being. Whether it does so equitably is now a governance question, not a technical one.”

A roadmap for sustainability and equity

The report calls for a responsible AI ecosystem built on six principles: transparency; efficiency by design; equity and environmental justice; lifecycle responsibility; global cooperation; and sustainable use. Practical recommendations are directed at each major group of stakeholders:

  • Governments should integrate AI infrastructure into energy planning, water governance, and land-use permitting, and require standardized environmental footprint reporting.
  • Industry and AI developers should treat model selection, default outputs, and routing decisions as footprint determinants, and improve efficiency by design.
  • Users and deploying organizations should adopt fit-for-purpose use — selecting the lightest model and lowest-energy format that meets the task.
  • Data center operators and utilities should treat siting and energy procurement as environmental footprint decisions and apply cumulative impact assessment.
  • Investors should treat electricity, carbon, water, and land footprints as material risks in AI infrastructure portfolios.
  • Communities and civil society should be involved early in data center siting decisions, with enforceable transparency and grievance mechanisms.
  • International institutions should support harmonized measurement standards, reduce incentives for cross-border burden shifting, and build compute capacity in excluded regions.

REPORT IN BRIEF

AI’s environmental cost is being mismeasured. Most current assessments focus on carbon emissions from training. The report argues this misses a substantial part of the picture. Every kilowatt-hour of AI electricity also carries a water footprint, from cooling and generation, and a land footprint, from infrastructure and supply chains. These three footprints can move in opposite directions, so reducing one can magnify another.

Data centres are becoming country-scale consumers of electricity, water and land. Global data-centre electricity use, estimated at 448 TWh in 2025, could reach 945 TWh by 2030. The associated water footprint is projected at 9.3 trillion litres and the associated land footprint at over 14,500 square kilometres.

Inference, not training, drives most of AI’s energy use. Once a model is deployed, billions of daily user interactions consume an estimated 80 to 90 per cent of its total energy. ChatGPT alone is estimated to process around 2.5 billion prompts per day.

Per-query energy varies by orders of magnitude across tasks. A typical chat query uses around 200 times the energy of basic text classification. An AI image uses around 1,450 times. A single short AI video can match 200,000 spam classifications. Model choice and product defaults are footprint decisions.

Energy and water required to generate AI images and videos. The energy required to generate a typical AI image is enough to power a 10-watt LED bulb for 17 minutes, and the energy required for a high-complexity AI video is sufficient to run that same bulb for 42 hours. Similarly, the electricity-associated water footprint is about two tablespoons (29 mL) for a single image, but jumps to 4.1 liters for a complex video—almost equivalent to a two-day drinking water need for one person.

Efficiency improvements alone will not contain growth. The report cites the rebound effect, sometimes called the Jevons Paradox, to explain why per-query gains are typically absorbed by rising volumes. Caps on tokens, resolution and output length are needed alongside efficiency.

AI compute is geographically concentrated. Only 32 countries host AI-specialised data centres. Over 90 per cent of capacity is in two countries. More than 150 countries currently lack sovereign AI compute infrastructure.

The hardware lifecycle is the next frontier. AI infrastructure could generate up to 2.5 million tonnes of electronic waste each year by 2030. Critical minerals required for AI hardware are concentrated in regions with weaker environmental oversight, often in the Global South.

A six-principle governance framework. The report proposes a “responsible AI ecosystem” built on transparency, efficiency by design, equity and environmental justice, lifecycle responsibility, global cooperation, and sustainable use, with specific responsibilities assigned across the AI ecosystem.

KEY POLICY MESSAGES

Carbon-only metrics are no longer sufficient for AI. Disclosure standards for AI’s environmental impact should require carbon, water and land footprints jointly, in standardised units, across both training and inference and across jurisdictions, so that regulators and investors can compare like with like.

Inference deserves the policy attention that training has received. Because operational use accounts for the majority of AI energy demand, governance should focus on product defaults, model selection and behavioural levers, not only on the largest training runs.

Siting decisions are environmental decisions. Where data centres are built, and from which grid they draw power, determines the carbon, water and land profile of the same workload. Permitting, environmental impact assessment and community consultation should reflect this reality.

Local capacity-planning needs to keep pace with global compute geography. The Irish, Mexican and Uruguayan cases described in the report show what happens when grid and water systems are asked to absorb workloads that serve users elsewhere. Transparent mitigation and benefit-sharing should accompany expansion.

Efficiency gains require demand-side guardrails. Without resource budgets, token-per-prompt limits, default low-resolution settings and similar guardrails, efficiency improvements will be absorbed by volume growth.

AI compute access is itself an equity issue. More than 150 countries currently lack sovereign AI compute. International institutions can help by supporting capacity-building, harmonising disclosure, and reducing incentives for cross-border burden-shifting.

The full value chain requires governance. Critical-mineral extraction at the upstream end and electronic waste at the downstream end are integral to AI’s footprint and currently fall on communities that capture little of the benefit.

Investors and financial institutions can move first. Treating carbon, water and land footprints as material risks in due diligence on AI infrastructure portfolios is described in the report as one of the fastest available levers.

AI within planetary limits is achievable. The report’s central argument is constructive. Capability and stewardship can grow together, but only with measurement, transparency, and shared responsibility across the ecosystem.

REPORT INFORMATION

Interview requests should be submitted to media.inweh@unu.edu

ABOUT UNU-INWEH

Marking its 30th anniversary of operation in 2026, the United Nations University Institute for Water, Environment and Health (UNU-INWEH) is one of 13 institutions that make up the United Nations University (UNU), the academic arm of the UN. Known as ‘The UN’s Think Tank on Water’, UNU-INWEH addresses critical water, environmental, and health challenges around the world. Through research, training, capacity development, and knowledge dissemination, the institute contributes to solving pressing global sustainability and human security issues of concern to the UN and its Member States. Headquartered in Richmond Hill, Ontario, UNU-INWEH has been hosted and supported by the Government of Canada since 1996. With a global mandate and extensive partnerships across UN entities, international organizations, and governments, UNU-INWEH operates through its UNU Hubs in Calgary, Hamburg, New York, Lund, and Pretoria, and an international network of affiliates.

blocks.html_en: The report finds that AI’s environmental cost is being systematically mismeasured. Most existing assessments focus on the carbon emissions associated with training large models. Yet every kilowatt-hour of electricity used to train or run an AI system also carries a water footprint, from cooling and power generation, and a land footprint, from energy infrastructure and supply chains. These three footprints do not move in the same direction. Switching from coal to bioenergy, for example, can on average cut the carbon footprint of electricity by 70 per cent, while increasing its water footprint more than thirty-fold and its land footprint a hundred-fold. The report concludes that “low-carbon” is not automatically “low-water” or “low-land” and warns that evaluating AI sustainability through a single metric can hide trade-offs and shift environmental burdens onto regions already facing water or land stress.

blocks.html_en: Public discussion has largely focused on the energy required to train massive models. Training GPT-3 was estimated to require 1.3 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of electricity, while estimates suggest GPT-4 consumed between 50 and 70 GWh. However, the report reveals this framing is outdated. sentences.en: The report calls for a responsible AI ecosystem built on six principles: transparency; efficiency by design; equity and environmental justice; lifecycle responsibility; global cooperation; and sustainable use.
sentences.zh: 该报告呼吁建立一个基于六项原则的负责任的人工智能生态系统：透明度；设计效率；公平和环境正义；生命周期责任；全球合作；和可持续利用。

sentences.en: Practical recommendations are directed at each major group of stakeholders:
sentences.zh: 实用建议针对每个主要利益相关者群体：

blocks.html_en: • Governments should integrate AI infrastructure into energy planning, water governance, and land-use permitting, and require standardized environmental footprint reporting.

sentences.en: Governments should integrate AI infrastructure into energy planning, water governance, and land-use permitting, and require standardized environmental footprint reporting.
sentences.zh: 政府应将人工智能基础设施纳入能源规划、水治理和土地使用许可，并要求标准化的环境足迹报告。

blocks.html_en: • Industry and AI developers should treat model selection, default outputs, and routing decisions as footprint determinants, and improve efficiency by design.

sentences.en: Industry and AI developers should treat model selection, default outputs, and routing decisions as footprint determinants, and improve efficiency by design.
sentences.zh: 行业和人工智能开发人员应将模型选择、默认输出和路由决策视为足迹决定因素，并通过设计提高效率。

blocks.html_en: • Users and deploying organizations should adopt fit-for-purpose use — selecting the lightest model and lowest-energy format that meets the task.

sentences.en: Users and deploying organizations should adopt fit-for-purpose use — selecting the lightest model and lowest-energy format that meets the task.
sentences.zh: 用户和部署组织应采用适合用途的用途——选择满足任务的最轻模型和最低能耗格式。

blocks.html_en: • Data center operators and utilities should treat siting and energy procurement as environmental footprint decisions and apply cumulative impact assessment.

sentences.en: Data center operators and utilities should treat siting and energy procurement as environmental footprint decisions and apply cumulative impact assessment.
sentences.zh: 数据中心运营商和公用事业公司应将选址和能源采购视为环境足迹决策，并应用累积影响评估。

blocks.html_en: • Investors should treat electricity, carbon, water, and land footprints as material risks in AI infrastructure portfolios.

sentences.en: Investors should treat electricity, carbon, water, and land footprints as material risks in AI infrastructure portfolios.
sentences.zh: 投资者应将电力、碳、水和土地足迹视为人工智能基础设施投资组合的重大风险。

blocks.html_en: • Communities and civil society should be involved early in data center siting decisions, with enforceable transparency and grievance mechanisms.

sentences.en: Communities and civil society should be involved early in data center siting decisions, with enforceable transparency and grievance mechanisms.
sentences.zh: 社区和民间社会应尽早参与数据中心选址决策，并制定可执行的透明度和申诉机制。

blocks.html_en: • International institutions should support harmonized measurement standards, reduce incentives for cross-border burden shifting, and build compute capacity in excluded regions.

sentences.en: International institutions should support harmonized measurement standards, reduce incentives for cross-border burden shifting, and build compute capacity in excluded regions.
sentences.zh: 国际机构应支持统一的衡量标准，减少跨境负担转移的激励，并在排除地区建立计算能力。

blocks.html_en: AI’s environmental cost is being mismeasured. Most current assessments focus on carbon emissions from training. The report argues this misses a substantial part of the picture. Every kilowatt-hour of AI electricity also carries a water footprint, from cooling and generation, and a land footprint, from infrastructure and supply chains. These three footprints can move in opposite directions, so reducing one can magnify another.

sentences.en: AI’s environmental cost is being mismeasured.
sentences.zh: 人工智能的环境成本被错误衡量。

sentences.en: Most current assessments focus on carbon emissions from training.
sentences.zh: 目前大多数评估都集中在培训产生的碳排放上。

sentences.en: The report argues this misses a substantial part of the picture.
sentences.zh: 报告认为，这种说法忽略了大部分情况。

sentences.en: Every kilowatt-hour of AI electricity also carries a water footprint, from cooling and generation, and a land footprint, from infrastructure and supply chains.
sentences.zh: 每千瓦时的人工智能电力还带有来自冷却和发电的水足迹，以及来自基础设施和供应链的土地足迹。

sentences.en: These three footprints can move in opposite directions, so reducing one can magnify another.
sentences.zh: 这三个足迹可以向相反的方向移动，因此减少一个足迹可以放大另一个足迹。

blocks.html_en: Data centres are becoming country-scale consumers of electricity, water and land. Global data-centre electricity use, estimated at 448 TWh in 2025, could reach 945 TWh by 2030. The associated water footprint is projected at 9.3 trillion litres and the associated land footprint at over 14,500 square kilometres.

sentences.en: Data centres are becoming country-scale consumers of electricity, water and land.
sentences.zh: 数据中心正在成为国家级的电力、水和土地消耗者。

sentences.en: Global data-centre electricity use, estimated at 448 TWh in 2025, could reach 945 TWh by 2030.
sentences.zh: 预计 2025 年全球数据中心用电量为 448 太瓦时，到 2030 年可能达到 945 太瓦时。

sentences.en: The associated water footprint is projected at 9.3 trillion litres and the associated land footprint at over 14,500 square kilometres.
sentences.zh: 相关水足迹预计为 9.3 万亿升，相关土地足迹超过 14,500 平方公里。

blocks.html_en: Inference, not training, drives most of AI’s energy use. Once a model is deployed, billions of daily user interactions consume an estimated 80 to 90 per cent of its total energy. ChatGPT alone is estimated to process around 2.5 billion prompts per day.

sentences.en: Inference, not training, drives most of AI’s energy use.
sentences.zh: 人工智能的大部分能源消耗是由推理而非训练驱动的。

sentences.en: Once a model is deployed, billions of daily user interactions consume an estimated 80 to 90 per cent of its total energy.
sentences.zh: 一旦部署模型，每天数十亿次用户交互估计会消耗其总能量的 80% 到 90%。

sentences.en: ChatGPT alone is estimated to process around 2.5 billion prompts per day.
sentences.zh: 据估计，仅 ChatGPT 每天就处理约 25 亿条提示。

blocks.html_en: Per-query energy varies by orders of magnitude across tasks. A typical chat query uses around 200 times the energy of basic text classification. An AI image uses around 1,450 times. A single short AI video can match 200,000 spam classifications. Model choice and product defaults are footprint decisions.

sentences.en: Per-query energy varies by orders of magnitude across tasks.
sentences.zh: 每个查询的能量在任务之间存在数量级的差异。

sentences.en: A typical chat query uses around 200 times the energy of basic text classification.
sentences.zh: 典型的聊天查询使用的能量大约是基本文本分类的 200 倍。

sentences.en: An AI image uses around 1,450 times.
sentences.zh: 一张 AI 图像的使用次数约为 1,450 次。

sentences.en: A single short AI video can match 200,000 spam classifications.
sentences.zh: 单个AI短视频可匹配20万条垃圾邮件分类。

sentences.en: Model choice and product defaults are footprint decisions.
sentences.zh: 型号选择和产品默认值是足迹决策。

blocks.html_en: Energy and water required to generate AI images and videos. The energy required to generate a typical AI image is enough to power a 10-watt LED bulb for 17 minutes, and the energy required for a high-complexity AI video is sufficient to run that same bulb for 42 hours. Similarly, the electricity-associated water footprint is about two tablespoons (29 mL) for a single image, but jumps to 4.1 liters for a complex video—almost equivalent to a two-day drinking water need for one person.

sentences.en: Energy and water required to generate AI images and videos.
sentences.zh: 生成人工智能图像和视频所需的能源和水。

sentences.en: The energy required to generate a typical AI image is enough to power a 10-watt LED bulb for 17 minutes, and the energy required for a high-complexity AI video is sufficient to run that same bulb for 42 hours.
sentences.zh: 生成典型 AI 图像所需的能量足以为 10 瓦 LED 灯泡供电 17 分钟，而高复杂性 AI 视频所需的能量足以让同一灯泡运行 42 小时。

sentences.en: Similarly, the electricity-associated water footprint is about two tablespoons (29 mL) for a single image, but jumps to 4.1 liters for a complex video—almost equivalent to a two-day drinking water need for one person.
sentences.zh: 同样，对于一张图像来说，与电力相关的水足迹约为两汤匙（29 毫升），但对于一个复杂的视频来说，水足迹会跃升至 4.1 升，几乎相当于一个人两天的饮用水需求。

blocks.html_en: Efficiency improvements alone will not contain growth. The report cites the rebound effect, sometimes called the Jevons Paradox, to explain why per-query gains are typically absorbed by rising volumes. Caps on tokens, resolution and output length are needed alongside efficiency.

sentences.en: Efficiency improvements alone will not contain growth.
sentences.zh: 仅靠效率提高并不能遏制增长。

sentences.en: The report cites the rebound effect, sometimes called the Jevons Paradox, to explain why per-query gains are typically absorbed by rising volumes.
sentences.zh: 该报告引用了反弹效应（有时称为杰文斯悖论）来解释为什么每次查询的收益通常会被不断增长的交易量所吸收。

sentences.en: Caps on tokens, resolution and output length are needed alongside efficiency.
sentences.zh: 除了效率之外，还需要对代币、分辨率和输出长度进行限制。

blocks.html_en: AI compute is geographically concentrated. Only 32 countries host AI-specialised data centres. Over 90 per cent of capacity is in two countries. More than 150 countries currently lack sovereign AI compute infrastructure.

sentences.en: AI compute is geographically concentrated.
sentences.zh: 人工智能计算在地理上是集中的。

sentences.en: Only 32 countries host AI-specialised data centres.
sentences.zh: 只有 32 个国家拥有人工智能专业数据中心。

sentences.en: Over 90 per cent of capacity is in two countries.
sentences.zh: 超过 90% 的产能位于两个国家。

sentences.en: More than 150 countries currently lack sovereign AI compute infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 目前有 150 多个国家缺乏主权人工智能计算基础设施。

blocks.html_en: The hardware lifecycle is the next frontier. AI infrastructure could generate up to 2.5 million tonnes of electronic waste each year by 2030. Critical minerals required for AI hardware are concentrated in regions with weaker environmental oversight, often in the Global South.

sentences.en: The hardware lifecycle is the next frontier.
sentences.zh: 硬件生命周期是下一个前沿领域。

sentences.en: AI infrastructure could generate up to 2.5 million tonnes of electronic waste each year by 2030.
sentences.zh: 到 2030 年，人工智能基础设施每年可能产生多达 250 万吨电子垃圾。

sentences.en: Critical minerals required for AI hardware are concentrated in regions with weaker environmental oversight, often in the Global South.
sentences.zh: 人工智能硬件所需的关键矿物集中在环境监管较弱的地区，通常是南半球。

blocks.html_en: A six-principle governance framework. The report proposes a “responsible AI ecosystem” built on transparency, efficiency by design, equity and environmental justice, lifecycle responsibility, global cooperation, and sustainable use, with specific responsibilities assigned across the AI ecosystem.

sentences.en: A six-principle governance framework.
sentences.zh: 六项原则的治理框架。

sentences.en: The report proposes a “responsible AI ecosystem” built on transparency, efficiency by design, equity and environmental justice, lifecycle responsibility, global cooperation, and sustainable use, with specific responsibilities assigned across the AI ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 该报告提出了一个建立在透明度、设计效率、公平和环境正义、生命周期责任、全球合作和可持续利用基础上的“负责任的人工智能生态系统”，并在整个人工智能生态系统中分配了具体的责任。

blocks.html_en: KEY POLICY MESSAGES

sentences.en: KEY POLICY MESSAGES
sentences.zh: 关键政策信息

blocks.html_en: Carbon-only metrics are no longer sufficient for AI. Disclosure standards for AI’s environmental impact should require carbon, water and land footprints jointly, in standardised units, across both training and inference and across jurisdictions, so that regulators and investors can compare like with like.

sentences.en: Carbon-only metrics are no longer sufficient for AI.
sentences.zh: 对于人工智能来说，仅碳指标已经不够了。

sentences.en: Disclosure standards for AI’s environmental impact should require carbon, water and land footprints jointly, in standardised units, across both training and inference and across jurisdictions, so that regulators and investors can compare like with like.
sentences.zh: 人工智能环境影响的披露标准应要求以标准化单位、跨训练和推理以及跨司法管辖区共同提供碳、水和土地足迹，以便监管机构和投资者可以进行同类比较。

blocks.html_en: Inference deserves the policy attention that training has received. Because operational use accounts for the majority of AI energy demand, governance should focus on product defaults, model selection and behavioural levers, not only on the largest training runs.

sentences.en: Inference deserves the policy attention that training has received.
sentences.zh: 推理值得像培训一样受到政策关注。

sentences.en: Because operational use accounts for the majority of AI energy demand, governance should focus on product defaults, model selection and behavioural levers, not only on the largest training runs.
sentences.zh: 由于操作使用占人工智能能源需求的大部分，治理应重点关注产品默认、模型选择和行为杠杆，而不仅仅是最大的训练运行。

blocks.html_en: Siting decisions are environmental decisions. Where data centres are built, and from which grid they draw power, determines the carbon, water and land profile of the same workload. Permitting, environmental impact assessment and community consultation should reflect this reality.

sentences.en: Siting decisions are environmental decisions.
sentences.zh: 选址决策就是环境决策。

sentences.en: Where data centres are built, and from which grid they draw power, determines the carbon, water and land profile of the same workload.
sentences.zh: 数据中心建在哪里，从哪个电网获取电力，决定了相同工作负载的碳、水和土地状况。

sentences.en: Permitting, environmental impact assessment and community consultation should reflect this reality.
sentences.zh: 许可、环境影响评估和社区咨询应反映这一现实。

blocks.html_en: Local capacity-planning needs to keep pace with global compute geography. The Irish, Mexican and Uruguayan cases described in the report show what happens when grid and water systems are asked to absorb workloads that serve users elsewhere. Transparent mitigation and benefit-sharing should accompany expansion.

sentences.en: Local capacity-planning needs to keep pace with global compute geography.
sentences.zh: 本地容量规划需要与全球计算地理保持同步。

sentences.en: The Irish, Mexican and Uruguayan cases described in the report show what happens when grid and water systems are asked to absorb workloads that serve users elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 报告中描述的爱尔兰、墨西哥和乌拉圭案例表明，当电网和供水系统被要求承担为其他地方的用户提供服务的工作量时会发生什么。

sentences.en: Transparent mitigation and benefit-sharing should accompany expansion.
sentences.zh: 透明的缓解和惠益分享应伴随着扩张。

blocks.html_en: Efficiency gains require demand-side guardrails. Without resource budgets, token-per-prompt limits, default low-resolution settings and similar guardrails, efficiency improvements will be absorbed by volume growth.

sentences.en: Efficiency gains require demand-side guardrails.
sentences.zh: 效率的提高需要需求方的护栏。

sentences.en: Without resource budgets, token-per-prompt limits, default low-resolution settings and similar guardrails, efficiency improvements will be absorbed by volume growth.
sentences.zh: 如果没有资源预算、每个提示的令牌限制、默认低分辨率设置和类似的护栏，效率的提高将被数量的增长所吸收。

blocks.html_en: AI compute access is itself an equity issue. More than 150 countries currently lack sovereign AI compute. International institutions can help by supporting capacity-building, harmonising disclosure, and reducing incentives for cross-border burden-shifting.

sentences.en: AI compute access is itself an equity issue.
sentences.zh: 人工智能计算访问本身就是一个公平问题。

sentences.en: More than 150 countries currently lack sovereign AI compute.
sentences.zh: 目前有 150 多个国家缺乏主权人工智能计算。

sentences.en: International institutions can help by supporting capacity-building, harmonising disclosure, and reducing incentives for cross-border burden-shifting.
sentences.zh: 国际机构可以通过支持能力建设、协调信息披露和减少跨境负担转移的激励措施来提供帮助。

blocks.html_en: The full value chain requires governance. Critical-mineral extraction at the upstream end and electronic waste at the downstream end are integral to AI’s footprint and currently fall on communities that capture little of the benefit.

content_html_zh:
联合国大学调查警告称，到 2030 年，人工智能的用水量将满足 13 亿人的需求，而其用电量将是 6.5 亿人的三倍

加拿大安大略省列治文山（2026 年 6 月 3 日）——到 2030 年，为人工智能提供动力的全球数据中心预计将消耗 945 太瓦时的电力。 这几乎是巴基斯坦、孟加拉国和尼日利亚年用电量的三倍，这三个国家的人口总数超过 6.5 亿。 它们相关的水足迹将相当于撒哈拉以南非洲地区全部 13 亿人口的基本年度生活用水需求，其土地足迹将超过 14,500 平方公里，大约是雅加达大都市面积的两倍，雅加达大都市面积超过 3200 万。

联合国大学水、环境与健康研究所 (UNU-INWEH) 的新报告《人工智能能源使用的环境成本：碳、水和土地足迹》详细介绍了这些严峻的发现。 研究人员此前曾对数据中心的温室气体排放发出过警告。 但联合国科学家现在认为，人工智能和数据中心的环境成本不能仅通过碳排放来理解。 在他们的报告中，他们量化了全球人工智能用电的碳足迹、水足迹和土地足迹，并强调了全球 20 个最大的数据中心枢纽中这些足迹之间的巨大差异。

领导调查小组的UNU-INWEH主任Kaveh Madani教授表示：“这份报告并不是反对人工智能，人工智能是一项正在改善全世界数十亿人生活的技术变革。” “这是呼吁负责任地使用它并积极解决其意外影响，以使其可持续和公平。 我们只有一个狭窄的窗口来确保我们这个时代的技术革命的支柱在地球极限内发展，并且为推进人工智能提供关键矿物的社区以及托管其基础设施和电子垃圾的社区也能从中受益。”

被错误测量的足迹

报告发现，人工智能的环境成本被系统性地错误衡量。 大多数现有评估都侧重于与训练大型模型相关的碳排放。 然而，用于训练或运行人工智能系统的每千瓦时电力也会带来来自冷却和发电的水足迹，以及来自能源基础设施和供应链的土地足迹。 这三个脚印的移动方向并不相同。 例如，从煤炭转向生物能源，平均可以将电力的碳足迹减少 70%，同时使水足迹增加三十倍以上，使土地足迹增加一百倍。 该报告的结论是，“低碳”并不自动意味着“低水”或“低土地”，并警告说，通过单一指标评估人工智能的可持续性可能会隐藏权衡，并将环境负担转移到已经面临水或土地压力的地区。

基础设施层面的数字迅速复合。 2025 年，全球数据中心消耗的电力预计为 448 太瓦时。 如果将其视为一个国家，它们将成为世界第 11 大电力消费国，仅次于法国，领先于沙特阿拉伯。

“最让我们惊讶的是，从碳角度来看最环保的选择往往对水或土地来说却是更糟糕的，”UNU-INWEH 研究员、该报告的主要作者米里亚姆·阿泽尔 (Miriam Aczel) 博士说。 “如果我们继续仅通过碳来判断人工智能的可持续性，我们可能会认为可再生能源使人工智能基础设施变得清洁，但这在解决一个问题的同时也造成了其他问题，而且通常是在没有要求的地方。”

推理、效率和反弹效应

公众讨论主要集中在训练大规模模型所需的能量上。 训练 GPT-3 估计需要 1.3 吉瓦时 (GWh) 的电力，而估计 GPT-4 消耗的电力在 50 到 70 GWh 之间。 然而，报告显示这一框架已经过时。 一旦部署了模型，推理（持续运行模型来回答日常用户提示）就成为主要成本，占人工智能总能耗的 80% 到 90%。 据估计，仅 ChatGPT 每天就处理约 25 亿条提示，相当于单个产品每年约 38​​3 GWh 的电力。 抵消相关的碳排放需要 10 年种植 260 万棵树苗，这些树苗足以覆盖曼哈顿大小的土地面积。 水足迹相当于撒哈拉以南非洲地区约 50 万人每年的最低生活用水需求，土地足迹相当于 800 多个足球场。

视频生成作为一种新兴的环境危机

每个查询的能量根据任务的不同而变化几个数量级。 典型的对话式聊天查询比基本文本分类消耗的能量大约高 200 倍。 生成单个 AI 图像可能需要该基线的 1,450 倍左右。 一个 AI 生成的短视频所消耗的电量相当于 200,000 个垃圾邮件分类的电量。 模型选择、提示长度、输出格式和分辨率都会对足迹产生重大影响。 然而，大多数这些决定都是在无形中做出的，用户永远看不到产品默认设置。

该报告援引了反弹效应（杰文斯悖论），警告说，随着模型变得更加高效，它们会变得更便宜并且使用更频繁。 如果没有对标记、分辨率或默认输出长度的明确限制，每个查询级别的改进很容易被数量的巨大增长所抵消。

“很多人认为，随着技术进步和流程变得更加高效，人工智能对环境的影响会减少。 但这只是整个问题的一部分。”该报告的合著者马达尼教授最近被任命为 2026 年斯德哥尔摩水奖获得者。 “更高效、更实惠的人工智能和能源意味着更多的人工智能消耗，使得整体足迹远远大于我们通过效率提升节省的成本。”

本地成本，远程收益

人工智能在全球大规模扩张的好处和负担是非常不平等的。 报告中的几个站点级案例展示了全球分布的人工智能服务如何造成巨大的本地压力。 在爱尔兰，到 2023 年，数据中心占总计量电力的 21%，超过所有城市家庭。 国家电网运营商已暂停都柏林周围的新审批，直到 2028 年，这使爱尔兰成为人工智能基础设施增长超过能源规划时会发生什么的具体、有记录的例子，也是其他国家走向的预览。

在墨西哥克雷塔罗，在长期干旱的情况下，不断扩大的计算基础设施正在利用水资源。 在乌拉圭，建设耗水量大的数据中心的计划恰逢 2023 年的干旱，这场干旱耗尽了蒙得维的亚的淡水储备，导致自来水无法安全饮用。

此外，到 2030 年，人工智能基础设施每年可能会产生多达 250 万吨电子废物，其中大部分是在保障措施有限的低收入经济体中处理的，而关键矿物是在环境监管薄弱的司法管辖区提取的。

UNU-INWEH 地理空间、气候和基础设施分析项目经理、该报告的合著者 Mir Matin 博士表示：“如果根据水资源压力最严重的地区绘制数据中心建设地点的地图，您往往会在某些情况下看到相同的区域。” “居住在这些地点附近的社区不一定是使用在那里运行的人工智能的社区。 这种不对称就是问题所在。 如果不解决这个问题，我们只会重复旧的模式，一些地方承担成本，另一些地方获得收益。”

数字鸿沟：AI计算90%集中在两个国家

虽然人工智能基础设施会带来环境成本，但它们也具有重大的经济、安全和主权优势，鼓励富裕国家建设更多数据中心。 世界上只有 32 个国家拥有人工智能专用数据中心，其中 90% 的容量集中在 2 个国家，而目前有 150 多个国家很少或根本无法获得主权人工智能计算。 该报告将这不仅视为经济鸿沟，而且视为环境正义问题：被排除在外的国家承担着关键的矿物开采和电子废物负担，而战略利益则流向其他地方。

联合国大学校长兼联合国副秘书长齐利齐·马尔瓦拉教授表示：“构建人工智能的全球系统还必须对其进行可持续和公平的管理。” “人工智能基础设施集中发展在世界特权地区，正在造成巨大的数字鸿沟，对人工智能的公平发展构成深刻挑战。 人工智能无疑可以促进繁荣和人类福祉。 这样做是否公平现在是一个治理问题，而不是一个技术问题。”

可持续发展和公平路线图

该报告呼吁建立一个基于六项原则的负责任的人工智能生态系统：透明度；设计效率；公平和环境正义；生命周期责任；全球合作；和可持续利用。 实用建议针对每个主要利益相关者群体：

  • 政府应将人工智能基础设施纳入能源规划、水治理和土地使用许可，并要求标准化的环境足迹报告。
  • 行业和人工智能开发人员应将模型选择、默认输出和路由决策视为足迹决定因素，并通过设计提高效率。
  • 用户和部署组织应采用适合用途的用途——选择满足任务的最轻模型和最低能耗格式。
  • 数据中心运营商和公用事业公司应将选址和能源采购视为环境足迹决策，并应用累积影响评估。
  • 投资者应将电力、碳、水和土地足迹视为人工智能基础设施投资组合的重大风险。
  • 社区和民间社会应尽早参与数据中心选址决策，并制定可执行的透明度和申诉机制。
  • 国际机构应支持统一的衡量标准，减少跨境负担转移的激励，并在排除地区建立计算能力。

简要报告

人工智能的环境成本被错误衡量。 目前大多数评估都集中在培训产生的碳排放上。 报告认为，这种说法忽略了大部分情况。 每千瓦时的人工智能电力还带有来自冷却和发电的水足迹，以及来自基础设施和供应链的土地足迹。 这三个足迹可以向相反的方向移动，因此减少一个足迹可以放大另一个足迹。

数据中心正在成为国家级的电力、水和土地消耗者。 预计 2025 年全球数据中心用电量为 448 太瓦时，到 2030 年可能达到 945 太瓦时。 相关水足迹预计为 9.3 万亿升，相关土地足迹超过 14,500 平方公里。

人工智能的大部分能源消耗是由推理而非训练驱动的。 一旦部署模型，每天数十亿次用户交互估计会消耗其总能量的 80% 到 90%。 据估计，仅 ChatGPT 每天就处理约 25 亿条提示。

每个查询的能量在任务之间存在数量级的差异。 典型的聊天查询使用的能量大约是基本文本分类的 200 倍。 一张 AI 图像的使用次数约为 1,450 次。 单个AI短视频可匹配20万条垃圾邮件分类。 型号选择和产品默认值是足迹决策。

生成人工智能图像和视频所需的能源和水。 生成典型 AI 图像所需的能量足以为 10 瓦 LED 灯泡供电 17 分钟，而高复杂性 AI 视频所需的能量足以让同一灯泡运行 42 小时。 同样，对于一张图像来说，与电力相关的水足迹约为两汤匙（29 毫升），但对于一个复杂的视频来说，水足迹会跃升至 4.1 升，几乎相当于一个人两天的饮用水需求。

仅靠效率提高并不能遏制增长。 该报告引用了反弹效应（有时称为杰文斯悖论）来解释为什么每次查询的收益通常会被不断增长的交易量所吸收。 除了效率之外，还需要对代币、分辨率和输出长度进行限制。

人工智能计算在地理上是集中的。 只有 32 个国家拥有人工智能专业数据中心。 超过 90% 的产能位于两个国家。 目前有 150 多个国家缺乏主权人工智能计算基础设施。

硬件生命周期是下一个前沿领域。 到 2030 年，人工智能基础设施每年可能产生多达 250 万吨电子垃圾。 人工智能硬件所需的关键矿物集中在环境监管较弱的地区，通常是南半球。

六项原则的治理框架。 该报告提出了一个建立在透明度、设计效率、公平和环境正义、生命周期责任、全球合作和可持续利用基础上的“负责任的人工智能生态系统”，并在整个人工智能生态系统中分配了具体的责任。

关键政策信息

对于人工智能来说，仅碳指标已经不够了。 人工智能环境影响的披露标准应要求以标准化单位、跨训练和推理以及跨司法管辖区共同提供碳、水和土地足迹，以便监管机构和投资者可以进行同类比较。

推理值得像培训一样受到政策关注。 由于操作使用占人工智能能源需求的大部分，治理应重点关注产品默认、模型选择和行为杠杆，而不仅仅是最大的训练运行。

选址决策就是环境决策。 数据中心建在哪里，从哪个电网获取电力，决定了相同工作负载的碳、水和土地状况。 许可、环境影响评估和社区咨询应反映这一现实。

本地容量规划需要与全球计算地理保持同步。 报告中描述的爱尔兰、墨西哥和乌拉圭案例表明，当电网和供水系统被要求承担为其他地方的用户提供服务的工作量时会发生什么。 透明的缓解和惠益分享应伴随着扩张。

效率的提高需要需求方的护栏。 如果没有资源预算、每个提示的令牌限制、默认低分辨率设置和类似的护栏，效率的提高将被数量的增长所吸收。

人工智能计算访问本身就是一个公平问题。 目前有 150 多个国家缺乏主权人工智能计算。 国际机构可以通过支持能力建设、协调信息披露和减少跨境负担转移的激励措施来提供帮助。

整个价值链需要治理。 上游端的关键矿物开采和下游端的电子废物是人工智能足迹不可或缺的一部分，目前落在了几乎没有获得好处的社区身上。

投资者和金融机构可以先行动。 报告称，在人工智能基础设施投资组合尽职调查中，将碳、水和土地足迹视为重大风险是最快的可用杠杆之一。

在地球极限范围内的人工智能是可以实现的。 报告的中心论点是建设性的。 能力和管理可以共同发展，但前提是整个生态系统具有衡量、透明度和共同责任。

关于UNU-INWEH

联合国大学水、环境与健康研究所 (UNU-INWEH) 将于 2026 年迎来成立 30 周年，它是联合国学术部门联合国大学 (UNU) 的 13 个机构之一。 UNU-INWEH 被称为“联合国水智库”，致力于解决世界各地严峻的水、环境和健康挑战。 通过研究、培训、能力发展和知识传播，该研究所致力于解决联合国及其会员国关注的紧迫的全球可持续发展和人类安全问题。 UNU-INWEH 总部位于安大略省列治文山，自 1996 年以来一直得到加拿大政府的主办和支持。 UNU-INWEH 拥有全球使命，并在联合国实体、国际组织和政府之间建立了广泛的合作伙伴关系，通过其位于卡尔加里、汉堡、纽约、隆德和比勒陀利亚的联合国大学中心以及国际附属机构网络开展运作。
